findings.source_quote: αὗται αἱ ἐντολαὶ σύμφοροί εἰσι τοῖς μέλλουσι μετανοεῖν
findings.english_quote: These commandments help those who are ready to repent[a].
findings.issue: “Ready to repent” introduces preparedness or willingness, whereas μέλλουσι μετανοεῖν identifies those who are about to repent. The simplified wording loses that prospective sense and substitutes a characterization of their disposition.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “These commandments help those who are about to repent[a].”

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against the supplied Greek throughout. The standard is acceptable against this working source; the simplified edition needs one correction. Both preserve the conditional warnings, negations, speaker changes, and contextual repentance terminology. Both retain brackets around “all,” corresponding to the source’s bracketed [πάντα], rather than presenting it as unqualified preserved text. This review does not authenticate the attributed edition, unseen manuscripts, or linked project records, and does not constitute scholarly certification.
